title: Indian Student Bilal Kazi Jailed 30 Years in UK for Grooming Girls Online
excerpt: Chester Crown Court jailed Bilal Kazi, 27, for 30 years plus eight years on extended licence. Police identified 70 victims aged 10 to 17 and say as many as 180 girls may have been targeted.
body:
• Bilal Kazi, 27, originally from Mumbai, was jailed for 30 years at Chester Crown Court, with a further eight years on extended licence, after grooming girls online while posing as a 14-year-old boy called “Reece”.
  • Police say 70 victims aged between 10 and 17 were identified across 28 of the UK's 45 police force areas, and as many as 180 girls may have been targeted.
  • Cheshire Police said the investigation was the force's largest ever online child sexual abuse case.
  • For parents in the diaspora, Cheshire Police's advice after sentencing was direct: speak to your children and take an interest in the apps and platforms they are using.

Bilal Kazi, a 27-year-old student originally from Mumbai, has been jailed for 30 years in Britain for grooming young girls online, Chester Crown Court heard. Kazi used a bogus photo and an online alias as a 14-year-old boy, “Reece”, posing as a boyfriend and pressuring victims, even while they were at school, to send naked photos and videos on Snapchat, according to PA reporting carried by the Glasgow Times.

He would then threaten to leak the images online, so victims sent more indecent images out of fear, the court heard. Police say Kazi targeted girls on apps including Snapchat, Wizz and Wink, and while playing Roblox. His youngest victim was aged 10, the PA report said.

What the court was told

The Glasgow Times, reporting PA, said Kazi admitted at an earlier hearing to 33 child sex offences relating to 19 victims, including causing a child to engage in penetrative sexual activity, making indecent images of children and six counts of blackmail, between 2021 and 2025. A Cheshire Constabulary account reproduced by Chester's Dee Radio put the plea differently in procedural terms: it said Kazi was charged with 39 offences as part of the Cheshire investigation, relating to offending between August 2021 and August 2025, pleaded guilty to 37 of the charges, with two left to lie on file.

Judge Steven Everett, Recorder of Chester, jailed Kazi for 30 years, with an extended sentence of eight years on licence. “You are a very dangerous person,” the judge said, according to the PA report. “He's taken away their childhoods.”

“You are a very dangerous person.”

— Judge Steven Everett, Recorder of Chester, as reported by PA

The court heard of the impact on victims. One girl said in a victim impact statement, after a video she sent was shared around her school: “I was young and I didn't know any better. I became a joke overnight, like I had done something wrong. I was just a kid.” The PA report said she lost all her friends, was bullied, fell into severe depression and took an overdose. Twice, indecent images were leaked online, leaving young victims suicidal, the court heard.

How the investigation unfolded

According to the Cheshire Police account, one victim reported the abuse to Derbyshire Police, and the investigation was taken over by Cheshire Constabulary's Online Child Abuse Investigation Team in May 2022, after enquiries established that Kazi's last known address was in Chester. He had left the country, and was arrested at Heathrow Airport in July 2023 when he returned to the UK, the PA report said.

Kazi, at the time living in Hubert Croft, Birmingham, while studying for a master's in chemical engineering, was on bail while police continued to investigate — but continued targeting teenage girls in the same way, the PA report said. He was finally rearrested and remanded into custody in August 2025. Police found hundreds of category A child sex abuse videos involving teenage girls, along with 9,000 messages exchanged with one girl alone in the space of three weeks, according to the same report.

Cheshire Police said 70 victims, aged between 10 and 17 at the time of Kazi's offending in the PA account, were identified across 28 of the UK's 45 police force areas, and officers identified 180 potential victims from data recovered from his device.

What police said after sentencing

Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of Cheshire Police's Online Child Abuse Investigation Team, said outside court: “There is a misconception that online offences have less impact on victims than crimes committed in person, but that could not be further from the truth.” She said many victims lived in constant fear of what Kazi would do if they failed to comply with his demands.

Detective Sergeant Ross Peel said victims should never feel ashamed, that responsibility lies solely with the offender, and urged parents to speak to their children and take an interest in the apps and platforms they use. That is the practical takeaway for Indian families in Britain and elsewhere: the platforms named in court — Snapchat, Wizz, Wink and Roblox — are the same apps children use every day, and police say offenders can target children from anywhere in the world.
image_caption: A Cheshire Police graphic shows Bilal Kazi and states he pleaded guilty to 37 charges of child sexual offences. Kazi was sentenced to 30 years in prison with a further eight years on extended licence at Chester Crown Court.
nri_angle: A Mumbai-origin student in Britain jailed in Cheshire Police's largest online child abuse case, with police urging parents to talk to children about the apps they use.
